value.title: Understanding defer and async in HTML Script Loading - Substack
value.snippet: Ordered Execution : Scripts with defer are executed in the order they appear in the document, which is useful for scripts that depend on each other. Supports DOMContentLoaded : Ensures that all deferred scripts execute before the DOMContentLoaded event, which is practical for scripts that need a fully parsed DOM.

value.title: Are deferred scripts executed before DOMContentLoaded event?
value.snippet: Deferred scripts have the advantage of downloading async , but executing in the order presented, which can be a problem with async (e.g. you can load your app bundle before your vendor bundle because you don't control the execution order of async scripts just by saying "in this order ").

value.title: HTMLScriptElement: defer property - Web APIs | MDN
value.snippet: The defer property of the HTMLScriptElement interface is a boolean value that controls how the script should be executed. For classic scripts , if the defer property is set to true, the external script will be executed after the document has been parsed, but before firing DOMContentLoaded event. For module scripts , the defer property has no effect.

value.title: Scripts: async, defer - Learn JavaScript | W3docs
value.snippet: The 'defer' attribute holds the script's execution until the HTML parser has finished its work, and then the script is executed. 'async' and 'defer' attributes run the scripts in the order they appear in the document.

value.title: Defer Scripts Execution Order: A Practical Guide to Cross-Browser ...
value.snippet: However, while ` defer ` is widely supported, subtle differences in how browsers like Chrome and Firefox process deferred scripts can lead to unexpected behavior. For example, execution order might break, or scripts might fire after ` DOMContentLoaded ` in one browser but not the other.

value.title: Document: DOMContentLoaded event - Web APIs | MDN
value.snippet: Note: document.readyState is set to "interactive" after the completion of the HTML parser but before the execution of scripts with defer or type="module". DOMContentLoaded is fired after the execution of these scripts , but before the execution of scripts with async . document.readyState is set to "complete" after the execution of async scripts .
